How to store fresh herbs

Soft herbs such as parsley, cilantro and dill keep best when treated like a bunch of flowers. Trim the stems, stand them in a jar with an inch of water and cover loosely with a bag before putting them in the fridge.

Hardy herbs such as rosemary, thyme and sage prefer to stay dry. Wrap them in a slightly damp paper towel, place them in a container and store them in the vegetable drawer.

Basil is the exception: it dislikes the cold and should be kept on the counter, away from direct sunlight, with its stems in water. Change the water every couple of days.

Freezing herbs

For longer storage, chop the herbs, pack them into an ice cube tray, cover with olive oil and freeze. The cubes can go straight into soups, sauces and stews.

Dried herbs lose their flavour within a year, so buy them in small quantities and keep them in airtight jars away from the heat of the stove.
